conclusion:
SPEED DEMON BENCHMARK ANALYSIS:
1. Per-Token Pipeline vs. Grammar Trigger: The per-token live-check pipeline (segmentation beam-search + spelling correction) averaged 0.817 ms/word, while the grammar trigger check averaged 0.007 ms/word (amortized per word). The segmentation + spelling layer adds ~0.810 ms of latency per word. This occurs because every out-of-vocabulary token invokes dynamic programming beam search over substrings followed by candidate set generation and frequency lookups. In contrast, the grammar check only triggers once every N=5 words on an established token window.
2. Method A vs. Method B Candidate Generation: Method B (Symmetric Delete) achieved an average latency of 0.006 ms/word compared to 0.126 ms/word for Method A, yielding a 19.7x speedup. Method A generates O(54L + 25) edit strings per word via deletions, transpositions, substitutions, and insertions, requiring extensive Python string creation. Method B precomputes a 1-character deletion dictionary over the vocabulary at startup, so at runtime it only generates L one-character deletions of the query string and performs O(1) hash map lookups. This dramatic reduction in string allocations makes Method B exceptionally well-suited for live editors.
3. Real-Time Feasibility: Because typical human typing speed is 40-80 WPM (~150-300 ms per keystroke/word), the per-token latency of 0.817 ms is orders of magnitude lower than the typing delay, confirming the editor operates seamlessly without perceptible lag.
